newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close shade higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close shade higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks recorded slim gains Thursday and were seen struggling higher as the week draws to a close.

"The market showed a very selective upward bias, driven chiefly by the steel sector. Many lagged behind, most notably cars, which were hit by selling by foreign players," said Humberto Lopez at traders Wainbuch.
He predicted prices would tick higher Friday but said the undertone remained cautious.
The blue-chip MerVal index closed up 0.4 percent at 840.45, trimming losses so far in the week to 1.2 percent.
"The bolsa looks pretty healthy, despite its current high valuations, but we have tomorrow's options expirations to deal with first," an analyst at an investment bank said.
"Then you have next Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, which causes some underlying tension, especially because long bond yields have been so erratic lately," he said.
Traders also said Monday's local holiday would encourage a trading lull Friday.
The broad market closed up 0.2 percent, with winners edging out losers 23 to 21 and 24 issues ending flat.
Floor volume picked up to 29.7 million pesos from 26.1 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover totaled 107.5 million pesos compared to 94.6 million Wednesday.
Best main-tier performers were construction stock Polledo, steelmaker Acindar and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which jumped 3.8 percent, 3.1 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively.
Losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, down 6.1 percent, and carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, off 5.3 percent and 4.6 percent, respectively.
